blurb: Where Sandboxes and sqlite Stores run. Default reads use the home's records only; a probe is --with live. machine.platforms moved to home get --with platforms.
reasons: Why reads are records only: today machine list and machine get probe every machine, up to 10 s, and a UI polls them. A state from the record costs nothing; --with live asks.
Why load_image: machine load reads as "load the machine". It copies a Docker reference from the host's Docker, not an archive file.
Why prune names what it removes: it removes one image, or with --unused every image no Sandbox uses. Nothing is removed by default.
Why an outdated worker needs two commands: machine start never replaces a worker of another build (#535 D11). The fix is machine stop, then machine start.
Why start and stop record an operation: today only the client that pressed Start knows the machine is starting. With an op in the record, every client answers busy.
Why stats stays a call: a UI polls it, and it writes no call-log line. --with space adds the one walk that says where the disk goes.

calls.note: today it probes every machine but native, up to 10 s in all; now it reads records and the probe is --with live. A row leaves state out when ready. Each item has machine.get's keys. Unpaged: a home holds a handful of machines

calls.new_work: The probe exists today and becomes opt-in; a records-only answer is new. The six states and the reason codes are new: today the record holds running, stopped or failed with a sentence in `error`, and the answer says running, stopped, failed, missing, unknown, creating, removing, unresolved or unsupported. The record must also keep the reason code a start found (`outdated` today is only a sentence) and when its state was last observed live, for `observed_at` on `unknown`.

calls.note: + machine.status. state comes from the machine's record, with no probe: ready (recorded running; native always), stopped, busy with op {name, phase, started_at} (name is create, start, stop or remove), or broken with reason (failed, outdated, unresolved, unsupported) and fix. Only --with live can answer engine_down (Docker not running; its fix is the host's own command that starts Docker), not_answering, missing, or unknown with observed_at. A machine is never blocked, so it has no blocked_by. message is the sentence behind a reason. supports lists what the platform does on this host (sqlite, postgresql_sandbox, log); memory_bytes and disk_bytes are the VM's size, null on a built-in machine

calls.note: was logs.machine. The first call answers the last --limit lines, oldest first; next_cursor continues with the lines before them and is left out at the start of the log. A call reads at most 64 KiB, so it may answer fewer lines; a line longer than that comes in pieces, each but the last with continued:true. At most 1000 lines. The log is the worker's own text: no time, level or source is parsed. Today's forward cursor (the lines after a place, to follow a log) is gone: a log pages backwards only, and a client that follows one reads the newest page again. native has no worker and is Unsupported; a worker that does not answer is Unavailable. It writes no call-log line, as today

calls.new_work: The call is new on the table; its own checks exist as today's off-table machine target. New: the shallow check of each Store and Sandbox on the machine in the same call (today one call is one target), the one answer shape (findings, not_checked, tree) in place of today's per-check report with pass, fail, unknown, skipped and blocked, a time budget per thing in place of one --timeout for the call, and one progress event per finished thing: {phase: self|stores|sandboxes, done, total, node}.
